technical_findings: All300 native slices verified against pinned source byte hashes, UID hierarchy and finite native decoding.
Five series150slices consistently taggedL, five separate series150slices with blank Laterality. Same five sequence descriptions recur; acquisition numbers2-6 versus8-12 distinguish two sets.
No exact decoded-pixel overlap between any series, so these are not byte-identical pixel duplicates.

In native coronal images, fibula appears on display-right in taggedL set and display-left in blank set. Both sets have row direction cosine x approximately+1 and column z approximately-1; no image flipping/reorientation was applied. Native axial views also show opposite lateral fibular positions.

Under standard human DICOM patient axes, columns here run toward patient-left. Fibular position therefore supports left knee for taggedL and right knee for blank-tag set, corroborating report separate RIGHT/LEFT examinations. This laterality inference combines anatomy and orientation, not missing-tag interpretation.
One pseudonymousPatientID acrossall300 does not independently prove patient identity. Ten distinct frame-of-reference hashes are not used to infer ten examinations or patients.
interpretation: Strong technical/visual evidence of both knees aggregated under one StudyInstanceUID. Do not treat all10series as one consistently left-sided knee or choose right by default for missing tags.
recommended_handling: Preserve source and bothseries sets. Keep this study outside single-knee report-supervised training until an explicit, validated series-to-knee policy and source-section adjudication are available. Do not invent whole-study OR labels or modify official gold.

orientation_reference.title: DICOM PS3.3 2026d C.7.6.2 Image Plane Module
orientation_reference.scope: For human BIPED coordinates, increasing x points patient-left; ImageOrientationPatient maps pixel row/column directions. This supports orientation interpretation, not a clinical diagnosis.

limitations: Only30selectednativeimages visually examined; all300 decoded and header/pixel-hash checked.
Stored orientation/laterality may themselves contain acquisition errors; independent technical review remains useful.
No diagnosis of tears/cartilage/marrow injury made from these images. Report thresholds and left postoperative ambiguity remain separate.
Existing report masks already supply no confident supervision; final release must preserve this exclusion or explicitly validate a series-level alternative.
